# Code of conduct

Clutch welcomes contributors of all backgrounds and experience levels. These
expectations apply to project issues, pull requests, reviews and other project
spaces, including maintainers' participation.

## Participate respectfully

- Be patient with questions and explain unfamiliar terms when helpful.
- Critique code and ideas using concrete evidence; respect the people involved.
- Accept corrections, acknowledge mistakes and give credit for others' work.
- Keep discussion relevant and allow others to participate.

Harassment, discriminatory remarks, personal attacks, threats, sexualized
content, spam and publishing another person's private information are unacceptable.
Repeated disruption or retaliation against someone raising a concern is also
unacceptable.

## Report a concern

Use GitHub's **Report content** controls on the relevant issue, PR or comment.
Choose **Report to repository admins** when available, or **Report abuse to GitHub
Support**. GitHub also provides a [support reporting form](https://support.github.com/contact/report-abuse).
See [GitHub's reporting guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam)
for available routes, including reports concerning a maintainer.

Do not open a public issue containing sensitive incident details or personal
information. Vulnerabilities in Clutch belong in the separate
[private security-reporting channel](SECURITY.md).

## Maintainer response

Maintainers review concerns in context and may clarify expectations, request a
change, remove harmful content, lock a discussion, or restrict participation.
Serious or repeated misconduct may result in a ban. Reports should be handled
with care and personal details shared only as needed to address the concern.
GitHub applies its own policies to reports sent to GitHub Support.
